newsitem.title: UK: Rank expanding UK pub-restaurant chain.
newsitem.headline: Rank expanding UK pub-restaurant chain.

text.p: Rank Group Plc is committed to expanding the Tom Cobleigh pub-restaurant chain and hopes to have almost 80 sites by the end of the year, chief executive Andrew Teare said on Thursday.
Speaking at the company's Annual General Meeting, Teare dismissed suggestions that Rank overpaid when it acquired the chain for a total of 123 million stg last October.

"Rank has added a truly exciting leisure product and an extremely valuable asset," Teare told shareholders. He added that the British leisure company previously had no exposure to the "eating-out" market, which he said was the fastest growing part of the sector at annual rates of seven-eight percent. Teare said that more than half of Tom Cobleigh's turnover came from food rather than beverage sales. Rank is expanding the chain from a base of 52 pub-restaurants.

Rank is also planning an aggressive expansion of the Hard Rock cafe brand, having taken control of the brand worldwide last year. Hard Rock managing director James Berk said that the company planned to launch a new venue each month for the next three years, the first set to open its doors in Baltimore on June 30.
Hard Rock is planning cafes in a further four U.S. cities plus one in Barcelona and three in the Middle East and three in Asia.
